A seat is one landing ticket in the harbor ledger, in quill ink, photographed at 600 dpi. The applicant files a fish buyer licence, a certified scale serial and a reef quay berth. The node reads the ink: stroke pressure, slant and paper grain differ per hand and sheet, so a traced copy fails, while a scale serial already filed is refused. Landings must fit the vessel's declared hold.

A certified scale runs 9,000 dollars, the licence 2,500, cold room 35,000, so fifty clones cost 2.3 million before one fish is weighed. Two boats land identical silver; ink says whose hand counted it.
